task: Fix the permission check failure after the LDAP group membership cache TTL was too long.

candidate_memories.content: Users added to the admin LDAP group cannot access admin features for up to 4 hours after group assignment.
The LDAP group membership cache TTL must be reduced from 4 hours to 5 minutes for security-sensitive groups.
The 4-hour TTL was set for read performance; group changes for admin groups are infrequent but must be immediate.
Only admin and security-sensitive group membership changes are delayed; standard group changes are not affected.
Session 5 note: the IT team submitted a ticket requesting immediate group membership propagation for admin users.
LDAP integration uses Active Directory with LDAPS for secure directory queries.
Session 8 note: the IT team migrated the LDAP directory to a new server in session 8.
Old practice: LDAP queries were made on every request before caching was introduced for performance.
The LDAP cache is implemented in Redis with per-group TTL configuration.
Session 3 note: the security team required that LDAP cache entries are encrypted at rest.
Old LDAP guide: the 4-hour TTL was set based on the LDAP directory's replication latency.
Security-sensitive group memberships must use short cache TTLs to prevent unauthorized access windows.
Session 12 note: the IT team added a change notification hook to the LDAP directory for real-time updates.
LDAP group membership changes are propagated to all LDAP replicas within 60 seconds.
A permission audit in session 6 confirmed no unauthorized access occurred with the current 4-hour TTL.
Non-admin LDAP groups have a 2-hour cache TTL; only admin groups use the 4-hour TTL.
Cache TTLs for permission data must be tunable per group class to balance performance and security.
Session 9 note: the security team added a LDAP group change audit log.
Old cache config: the uniform 4-hour TTL was set before per-group TTL configuration was supported.
The LDAP integration supports both on-premise Active Directory and Azure AD.
